research: [spread] Line opened Missouri -3 on Oct 4, peaked at -4.5, then came back to -3.5 (A&M +3.5 -115); it moved off the key number of 3 (WagerTalk preview, Oct 2026). Mild help to Texas A&M getting the hook.
[spread] Splits: Missouri had 67% of spread tickets, but Texas A&M had 56% of spread money after Missouri took 100% of early money (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Money-vs-tickets gap helps Texas A&M.
[spread] Total fell from 50.5 to 48.5 despite 100% of over money and tickets (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). A lower expected score makes 3.5 points worth more, which helps the underdog Texas A&M.

Missouri is out S JaDon Blair, RBs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman; seven more are questionable, incl. LB Robart Woodyard Jr. and S Kensley Louisdor-Faustin (On SI, Oct 9 injury report). Helps Texas A&M.

[angle] With Hardy and Fonoti out, RB Jamal Roberts carries the load: 606 rush yards (6th nationally) on 113 carries (2nd) (On SI, Oct 9). Helps Missouri if he holds up, but the backfield is one man deep.
Missouri QB Austin Simmons hasn't thrown an interception this season (On SI, Oct 9). Helps Missouri.
Texas A&M is without WR Terry Bussey and OL Blake Ivy; WR Mario Craver is questionable (On SI, Oct 9). Helps Missouri.
Missouri (4-1, No. 14) beat a top-10 Florida team last week (WagerTalk; On SI, Oct 9). Helps Missouri on form, though it's a possible emotional-letdown spot.
Texas A&M (3-2) snapped a two-game skid by beating Arkansas 34-7; Marcel Reed had no turnovers and hit seven receivers (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Texas A&M.
Texas A&M lost to Kentucky in Week 3 (WagerTalk). Helps Missouri: A&M isn't the 11-0 team of 2025.
[angle] Missouri managed only 230 total yards and 13 first downs vs Troy in Week 3 (WagerTalk). Its offense can stall, which helps Texas A&M.

[angle] Texas A&M won and covered the last three meetings, incl. 38-17 at Missouri in 2025 (outgained Mizzou 464-284), but Missouri had a backup QB then (WagerTalk). Old head-to-head; slight Texas A&M.
[angle] Drinkwitz said freshman OL DJ Jones is out and needs a heart transplant (WagerTalk). An emotional rallying point for Missouri at home; neutral to slight Missouri.
games.reasoning: Pre-game evidence was close: the market sat at -3.5 after touching -4.5, money split toward A&M while tickets were on Missouri, and Missouri was missing two running backs. That made A&M +3.5 a thin lean with Missouri projected by about 2. The most unusual angle was Missouri's lone healthy RB carrying a nation-high workload. A confirmed healthy Missouri backfield, or the line holding at -4.5, would have flipped it to a pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before deciding (see note).
games.contaminationNote: Before I had decided, a web-search summary quoted the 2026 Texas A&M Wikipedia season page as listing this game 'L 6-27 at Columbia' (Missouri winning 27-6). I recorded the lean the pre-game evidence pointed to (A&M +3.5), but it was locked after seeing the result.

research: [spread] The line was Oklahoma State -9.5 Tuesday with about 80% of tickets on OSU and no move (Heartland College Sports, Oct 6). DraftKings had -9.5 on Oct 7 (SI). FanDuel and this slate have -10.5 (FanDuel Research). So it moved up late toward OSU.
[spread] UCF is 4-1 ATS and has been within 10 points in every game this season (SI, Oct 7; Predictem, Oct 6). Helps UCF.
[spread] Oklahoma State is 3-1 ATS and 1-1 as a 10.5+ favorite; UCF is 1-0 ATS as a 10.5+ underdog (FanDuel Research). Mixed.
Since its Week 2 win over Oregon, Oklahoma State has outscored opponents 100-24, and it ranks No. 14 in adjusted defensive EPA/play (SI, Oct 7). Helps Oklahoma State.

Drew Mestemaker: 10 TD passes, 3 INTs and 300+ yards in each of his last three games, but 5 INTs this season; OSU has 8 turnovers in 4 games (SI; Predictem). Helps OSU, with turnover risk for UCF to exploit.

UCF's offense is 88th in adjusted EPA/play, outside the top 100 in success rate and 111th in EPA/pass (SI, Oct 7); 82nd in yards per play vs OSU's top 15 (Heartland). Helps Oklahoma State: a big underdog has to be able to score.
[angle] UCF is playing its sixth straight game without a bye and its second straight road game vs a ranked team; Oklahoma State comes off a bye (Heartland, Oct 6; SI). Helps Oklahoma State.
[angle] UCF blew a 17-0 third-quarter lead at Houston and lost 27-17 last week (Heartland, Oct 6). Helps Oklahoma State: UCF faded late.

UCF QB: Alonza Barnett is out (hamstring); Keyone Jenkins is probable, dealing with a high ankle sprain, and missed a series at Houston with cramps (Rotowire, Oct 7; Predictem). Starting C Jacob Maiava and LB Jayden Jennings are also hurt (Heartland). Helps Oklahoma State.

UCF's defense allows 17.6 ppg and ranks 27th in pass-efficiency defense (Heartland; FanDuel). OSU allows 19.8 ppg but ranks 96th in EPA/rush allowed, and UCF RB Duke Watson has 400+ yards (SI). Helps UCF stay close.
[angle] UCF won both previous meetings (45-3 in 2023, 17-14 in 2025), and this is UCF's first trip to Stillwater (Heartland). Old head-to-head; slight UCF.
The previews split: SI/DraftKings (Dewey) and Heartland (31-16) picked OSU to cover; Predictem took UCF +7.5; Dimers projected 31-21 (Heartland; Predictem; Dimers). Mixed.
games.reasoning: This season's efficiency numbers favored Oklahoma State by a wide margin (OSU's top-15 offense and defense vs a UCF offense outside the top 100 in success rate), and the situation agreed: OSU off a bye, UCF on its sixth straight game, banged up at QB and center. The line also rose from 9.5 to 10.5. UCF's 4-1 ATS record and within-10 streak kept it a lean, not strong. A healthy Barnett or a line move back below 10 would have made it a pass. CONTAMINATED: I saw the result before deciding (see note).
games.contaminationNote: Before I had decided, a web-search summary on Keyone Jenkins' injury status included a post-game headline: 'Oklahoma State surges past UCF 42-28 after a fumble-return turning point.' I locked the side the pre-game evidence pointed to, but it was locked after seeing the result.

research: Pitt QB Mason Heintschel tore his ACL in the 35-33 win at Virginia Tech on Oct 2 and is out for the season (Rotowire, Oct 2026). Helps North Carolina.

Backup Holden Geriner, who led the comeback at Virginia Tech, is 19-of-26 this season with no interceptions and gets his first start (Covers, Oct 10; Sportsgambler, Oct 8). Partly offsets the injury for Pitt.

[spread] Covers (Oct 10) says the market 'dropped' Pitt after the Heintschel injury, to -3.5, and calls it an overreaction. A line move on injury news is information, so this helps North Carolina relative to the old number.
[spread] Pitt is 4-1 ATS and 3-1 ATS as a 3.5+ favorite; North Carolina has 2 ATS wins in 4 games and is 2-1 as a 3.5+ underdog (FanDuel Research). Helps Pittsburgh.
[spread] Pitt has covered -3.5 in four straight home games and in 7 of its last 10 at home (Sportsgambler, Oct 8). Helps Pittsburgh.
Pitt is 4-0 at home, outscoring opponents 157-34, and hasn't allowed a third-quarter point (Covers, Oct 10). Helps Pittsburgh.

North Carolina scores 24.0 ppg (117th) and ranks 99th in rushing at 135.5 ypg; Billy Edwards Jr. went 13-of-30 for 135 yards at Clemson (Predictem, Oct 7; FanDuel). Helps Pittsburgh: the underdog has a weak offense.
[angle] Belichick's UNC defense allows 19.5 ppg (25th), 200.5 pass ypg (30th), and held TCU to 10 (Predictem, Oct 7). Facing a first-start backup QB is its best matchup. Helps North Carolina.
North Carolina has been outscored 26-9 in fourth quarters and has lost four straight conference games (Covers, Oct 10). Helps Pittsburgh.

[angle] Opponents have 38 rushing first downs against UNC, vs 31 total first downs for UNC's offense; UNC allows 152.5 rush ypg while Pitt runs for 162 ypg with 31:38 time of possession (Covers, Oct 10). Pitt can win without asking Geriner to throw a lot. Helps Pittsburgh.
Pitt's pass defense ranks 110th and allowed 434 passing yards at Virginia Tech (Predictem; Covers). Helps North Carolina's passing game (Edwards threw 3 TDs vs Notre Dame).
[angle] Under Narduzzi, Pitt has gained 400+ yards in seven of nine meetings with North Carolina (Covers, Oct 10). Old head-to-head; slight Pittsburgh.
The total moved from 47.5 (FanDuel, Predictem) to 46.5 (Covers, Oct 10), a low-scoring setup that makes +3.5 more valuable. Slight North Carolina.
games.reasoning: This season's data favored Pitt (4-1 ATS, dominant at home, a strong run game against a UNC defense that bleeds rushing first downs), and UNC's offense ranks 117th in scoring. The Heintschel injury had already been priced in when the line dropped to -3.5, so the lean was Pitt by about 5. The surprising angle was UNC's offense trailing its opponents' rushing first downs alone. A worse report on Geriner's readiness, or sharp money on UNC, would have made it a pass. Contaminated: see note.
games.contaminationNote: Before I had decided, a search summary from Rotowire showed later items: Geriner 'mistake-prone in first start... picked off twice' (almost certainly this game) and 'since losing [Heintschel] Pitt is 1-4 straight up and against the spread'. That isn't this game's score, but it strongly hints Pitt may have lost and failed to cover. I locked the lean the pre-game evidence supported.

research: Both teams are 5-0 and 2-0 in the Big Ten; Indiana is No. 7 (Sportsgambler, Oct 8-10; Predictem, Oct 6). Neutral.

[spread] Indiana is 1-4 ATS, but its spreads were 20.5 to 57.5 points; it covered its first, 47-15 at Rutgers as a 24.5-point favorite (Covers, Oct 10). That ATS record comes from huge numbers, not a -7.5 spot, so it's weak evidence for Nebraska.
[spread] Nebraska is 4-1 ATS (FanDuel Research). Helps Nebraska.

[spread] FanDuel priced Indiana -7.5 at -120 (Nebraska +7.5 -102), and Sportsgambler's odds board showed -8.5, so the price was moving toward Indiana. Covers (Oct 10) said early Kalshi action was on Nebraska. The market moving toward the favorite helps Indiana.
Indiana allows 237.8 yards per game (4th), 64.4 rushing ypg, and only six TDs in five games; it allows 10.8 ppg (7th) (Predictem, Oct 6; FanDuel). Helps Indiana.

[angle] Nebraska's 43.6 ppg came against Ohio (49), Bowling Green (56), Michigan State (31) and Maryland (48-23) (Predictem; Sportsgambler). Indiana's defense is far better than anything it has faced. Helps Indiana.
[angle] Lookahead: Indiana traveled from New Jersey (Rutgers) to Lincoln and hosts No. 5 Ohio State next week (Covers, Oct 10). Helps Nebraska.

Nebraska QB Anthony Colandrea threw for 238 yards and 3 TDs and ran for 108 vs Maryland; Nebraska is balanced at 231 rush / 244.6 pass ypg (Sportsgambler; Predictem). Helps Nebraska: a dual-threat can stress Indiana.
Indiana's Josh Hoover went 20-of-27 for 251 yards and 4 TDs at Rutgers; Indiana runs for 252.6 ypg (9th) vs a Nebraska run defense allowing just over 100 ypg (Predictem). Helps Indiana.

[angle] Indiana has won seven straight road games and is 8-2 in its last 10 on the road (Sportsgambler). Nebraska has won four straight at home and five straight overall under fourth-year coach Matt Rhule. Mixed, slight Indiana.
Nebraska's Carter Nelson (leg) was questionable for Indiana (Rotowire, Oct 8). Slight Indiana.
Indiana won the 2024 meeting 56-7 (Sportsgambler). Old head-to-head; slight Indiana.
Covers' Marchio and Predictem took Nebraska +7.5; numberFire gave Indiana 81.5% to win; Sportsgambler projected 31-21 Indiana. Mixed.
Weather: clear, low 80s in Lincoln (Covers). Neutral.
games.reasoning: This season's defensive numbers decided it: Indiana's top-5 defense against a Nebraska offense whose numbers came from a soft schedule, with the price drifting toward Indiana (-120 / -8.5). Indiana's 1-4 ATS record came from 20+ point spreads and doesn't carry over to -7.5. The surprising angle is the lookahead to Ohio State, which keeps this a lean rather than strong. Sharp money on Nebraska or a Hoover injury would have flipped it to a pass.
games.contaminationNote: No result seen. One preview page (Sportsgambler) had a current standings table showing later-season records (Indiana 9-2, Nebraska 7-4), which doesn't reveal this game's result.

research: South Carolina is 2-3, 0-3 in the SEC, has lost three straight, and has lost six straight road games (3-7 in its last 10 away) (Sportsgambler, Oct 8). Helps Florida.
[angle] Florida (4-1) is coming off its first loss, at Missouri, in Jon Sumrall's first season, and has won three straight at home (Sportsgambler; WagerTalk). A bounce-back home spot helps Florida.
[spread] Florida is 3-2 ATS and 1-1 as an 11.5+ favorite; South Carolina has one ATS win this season and is 0-1 as an 11.5+ underdog (FanDuel Research). Helps Florida.
[spread] Lines ranged from Florida -10.5 (Dimers; Sportsgambler odds board) to -12.5 (Pickswise) and -14 at one book (Dimers listing); this slate has -11.5. No clear sharp direction.
[spread] Dimers' model projects Florida 35-23 (12 points), almost exactly the line; numberFire gives Florida 72.2% to win (Dimers; FanDuel). Neutral.
Florida's defense allows 27.2 ppg (98th) and South Carolina scores 37.6 ppg (24th) (FanDuel Research). A backdoor route for South Carolina.
Florida scores 46.2 ppg (6th) against a South Carolina defense allowing 26.8 (94th) (FanDuel Research). Helps Florida.
[angle] LaNorris Sellers was at risk of losing the starting job to Cutter Woods because of his struggles (Rotowire odds page, Oct 2026). Helps Florida.
Florida WR Vernell Brown (knee) was a game-time decision after missing the Missouri loss (Rotowire, Oct 2026). Helps South Carolina if he sits.
South Carolina's Quay'sheed Scott was out vs Florida (Rotowire). Slight Florida.
[angle] Both teams have gone over the total in 4 of 5 games and the total sits at 58.5-60.5 (FanDuel; Sportsgambler). A high-variance game makes an 11.5-point spread less predictable. Neutral.
Florida has won four of the last five meetings (Sportsgambler). Old head-to-head; slight Florida.
games.reasoning: The numbers favored Florida, but by about the spread: Dimers projected 12 vs 11.5, and Florida's leaky defense (98th) gives South Carolina's offense a backdoor route. With the projection within a point of the line and Vernell Brown's status undecided, it's a pass. A firm Sellers benching or line movement to -13 would have made it a Florida lean.
games.contaminationNote: No final result seen. An injury search showed a Rotowire item that Florida RB Duke Clark was hurt in the second quarter of this game and didn't return (in-game news, not the score). I had already settled on a pass from the pre-game numbers.

research: [spread] Spread opened Notre Dame -35.5 on Oct 4 and moved to -38.5 (WagerTalk); this slate has -39.5. Steady movement toward Notre Dame.
[spread] Notre Dame had 86% of spread money and 71% of tickets (WagerTalk). Money heavier than tickets on Notre Dame, so not just public action; helps Notre Dame.

[spread] Under Marcus Freeman, Notre Dame covered all three games as a five-touchdown-plus favorite, +12.8 points vs the spread in those games (Covers, Oct 10); it's 18-9-1 ATS in its last 28 as a double-digit favorite (Predictem, Oct 5). Helps Notre Dame.
[spread] Stanford is 0-13 ATS on the road and 6-22 ATS in its last 28 vs ranked teams (Predictem, Oct 5). Helps Notre Dame.

Stanford's three losses were by 39 at home to Miami, 28 at Duke and 54 at Wake Forest (57-3), an average margin of 40.3, and it scored single digits in all three (WagerTalk; Covers; Predictem). Helps Notre Dame.
Stanford ranks 131st in scoring (about 5 ppg in its losses) and 135th in rushing (Predictem, Oct 5). A big underdog needs to be able to score to cover; Stanford can't. Helps Notre Dame.
Notre Dame's defense ranks 1st in yards allowed, 4th vs the run and 7th in points allowed (Predictem, Oct 5). Helps Notre Dame.

Stanford's defense ranks 137th vs the pass, 133rd in points allowed and 134th in yards allowed; its tackles leader, LB Matt Rose, and LB Jahsiah Graham have missed games (Predictem, Oct 5). Helps Notre Dame.
C.J. Carr has 13 TD passes and 1 INT and is 7th nationally in passer rating (Predictem; Covers). Helps Notre Dame.
[angle] Lookahead: Notre Dame plays at top-10 BYU next week and hosts Miami after that; Carr may be rested late (Predictem, Oct 5). The main backdoor risk; helps Stanford.

[angle] Notre Dame's run game ranks 65th after losing Jeremiyah Love and Jadarian Price to the NFL (WagerTalk; Predictem), though freshman Jonaz Walton ran for 120 yards on 23 carries last week. A slower clock in garbage time could slightly help Stanford.

[angle] Notre Dame's 15-game winning streak has every win by 10+ points; it's 6th in first-half scoring (25.6) and 10th in first-half defense (6.8 allowed) (Predictem; Covers). It builds the lead early, before a lookahead matters. Helps Notre Dame.
Weather: mid-70s, 13 mph wind, no rain (Covers, Oct 10). Neutral.
games.reasoning: A 39.5-point underdog covers only if it can score, and Stanford has been held to single digits in every loss while ranking 131st in scoring. Meanwhile money (86%) pushed the line from 35.5 to 39.5 and Notre Dame has covered every five-TD spot under Freeman. The lookahead to BYU, and Carr possibly resting late, keeps it a lean at about Notre Dame by 45 rather than strong. If the line had reached 42+, or ND had confirmed resting starters early, it would have been a pass.
